Whether a function really belongs to the client beyond its name
Field and input naming, not asked explicitly

assumptions: Client prefix for this workspace is acme_ (five of eight functions use it).
Endpoint naming refers to endpoint path segments (endpoint_path), which also covers query names such as getCustomerProfile.
Flag-only means enforcement = advisory, active = true, as the skill's default for new policies.
Customer's pre-approval of the plan covers the policy file and the dry run, so no further confirmation was needed.
confusions: The skill says to show one plan and wait for a yes before building; the brief says the customer already approved, so I built in the same turn. This is fine, but the two instructions should say which one wins.

object.naming's object_kinds for name_kind object does not list query, so an endpoint's own name is judged only as endpoint_path. The skill does not say that plainly; I inferred it from the param description.

The plural rule has no native plural check; the catalogue's example uses suffixes ['s'] which the docs call literal text. Irregular plurals will be flagged without an allowlist. I did not add an allowlist (the skill says to add no exemption unless asked).
The template catalogue has no client-prefix or endpoint snake_case template, so the policy is hand-built from object.naming uses.
wished_for: A recipe for per-client prefix naming (a prefix parameter the team sets once per workspace).
A worked example of endpoint_path snake_case with the expected finding text, so the wording of findings can be checked before running evaluate.
why_confidence: The three rules use real object.naming params and parse, and the dry run shows the policy will be created. I have not run xano policy evaluate, so the expected findings are predictions from reading the workspace, not results. Plural detection is a heuristic that will over- and under-flag, and the prefix is an assumption.
